requirement:
CSS reports only `Comment` attachments. These include `/* … */` blocks and
`//` line comments recognized by the bundled CSS grammar.
rationale:
**Obligations.** `requirements.sdk.sources.css.attachments` says CSS reports only `Comment` attachments. Those include `/* … */` blocks and `//` line comments that the bundled CSS grammar recognizes.

**Test.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_classify_only_their_attachment_syntax]` is marked `{test}` for this requirement. Its `test.css` case uses the source `"/* block */\na { color: red; }\n// line\n"`.
- The test gathers every attachment on every outline item and sorts them by span start.
- It asserts exact equality with `[(Comment, "/* block */"), (Comment, "// line")]`.
- This covers both comment forms the requirement names: the block comment and the `//` line comment.
- The same assertion compares each attachment's kind, so any `Annotation` or `Other` attachment on CSS would fail it. That enforces the "only `Comment`" clause.
- The assertion also compares the exact span text, so a wrong span would fail too.

**Possible gap.** The source has no CSS construct such as an at-rule that a different implementation might wrongly report as an `Annotation`. I checked the CSS profile, `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/languages/css.rs#static[PROFILE]`, to see whether this matters. It sets `attaches: never`. In `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/mod.rs#impl[Builder<'tree, 'source>]/fn[finish]`, annotations come only from non-comment attached siblings. So CSS cannot produce them, and a test for that case would add little. I used the implementation only to judge whether this missing scenario matters. The expected behavior comes from the requirement text.

**Conclusion.** The test exercises both required comment syntaxes and asserts the exact kind and span of each attachment. I found no gap.
